explanation: Mutual mandatory references create a cycle. If each row needs the other to exist first, there is no straightforward insertion order that satisfies both constraints at once.

options.text: Either row may be impossible to insert first because each one needs the other to already exist.
The database will always automatically convert the relationship into many-to-many.
The foreign keys will be treated as optional, so no constraint problem occurs.
The tables must be merged into one table, or the design is invalid.

prompt: Two tables each require a mandatory foreign key to the other: `A` must reference exactly one `B`, and `B` must reference exactly one `A`. What is the main practical problem with this design when inserting new rows?
